target.title: fix(file-transfer): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in tar listing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from tar listing in `dir.fetch` entry validation could silently swallow archive listing results instead of failing closed, weakening the archive validation security boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

`node-invoke-policy.ts` spawns `tar -tzf` with pipe stdio to list archive entries. The original fix used a no-op error listener, but ClawSweeper identified that this could let a partially-read archive pass final policy validation if stdout emits an error after only part of the listing was read.

The updated fix converts output stream errors into `ARCHIVE_ENTRIES_UNREADABLE`, killing the tar child, matching the existing fail-closed pattern already used for timeouts and oversized output in the same function.

## User Impact

`dir.fetch` archive entry validation no longer risks silently accepting incomplete tar listings when output stream errors occur. Stream failures are now treated as unreadable archives, consistent with all other error paths in the function.

## Evidence

```text
$ git diff origin/main --stat
 extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/node-invoke-policy.ts | 10 +++++++++-
 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

$ npx oxlint extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/node-invoke-policy.ts
  -> 0 errors
```

- Each stream error now triggers `stopChild()` + `finish({ code: "ARCHIVE_ENTRIES_UNREADABLE", ... })`, matching the same finish signature used by timeout and oversized-output guards on lines 353-376.
- The existing `child.stdin.on("error", ...)` handler already uses `finish({ code: "ARCHIVE_ENTRIES_UNREADABLE", ... })` for stdin failures -- the new handlers extend the same fail-closed behavior to stdout and stderr.
